title: PoE2 0.2.1: 22 Runes, 7 Talismans, 15 Soul Cores, and How Unique Drops Changed
summary: 0.2.1 overhauled the loot and socketable systems: 22 Endgame Runes, 7 Talismans and 15 Soul Cores arrived, while Unique drops stopped considering Item Class, Mythic Uniques rose, and the party Unique bonus was cut.
description: An items and loot-system article for Path of Exile 2 0.2.1. It covers the new Runes, Talismans and Soul Cores, why your Item Filter needs new entries, and the four Unique-drop rule changes: no more Item Class weighting, a Mythic Unique increase, reduced Common Unique share in high-tier areas, and a smaller party bonus.
author: StratLore Editorial
imageAlt: Endgame Runes, Talismans and Soul Cores introduced in 0.2.1

sections.title: Quick summary
paragraphs: Patch 0.2.1 was the loot and socketable overhaul of the Dawn of the Hunt era. It introduced three whole new families of socketable items: 22 Endgame Runes, 7 Talismans, and 15 Soul Cores, each meant to be slotted into gear for new modifiers and build options.

Alongside the socketables, 0.2.1 rewrote how Unique items drop. The Unique generation pipeline stopped considering Item Class, which made Rings and Amulets show up more often. A Mythic Unique increase pushed more top-tier drops into circulation, high-tier areas began reducing the share of Common Uniques, and the party-play Unique bonus was reduced.

Console players got a quiet but important quality-of-life win: Item Filter support arrived, which matters directly because the new socketables will not appear in an old filter until you add entries for them. This article explains each change in player terms and flags what is still true versus what later patches may have adjusted.
No drop-rate percentages are stated here. The official notes describe these as rule changes, not published numbers, so every figure below is described by direction and mechanism only.
bullets: 0.2.1 added 22 Endgame Runes, 7 Talismans, and 15 Soul Cores.
Unique drops no longer consider Item Class, so Rings and Amulets are more common.
Mythic Unique drop rate increased; high-tier areas reduce Common Unique share.
Console Item Filter support means new socketables need filter entries.

cards.detail: A new Endgame-tier Rune family for slotted gear modifiers. Individual effects are not enumerated here; the count of 22 is the confirmed fact from the 0.2.1 notes.
A new Talisman socketable type added in 0.2.1. The confirmed count is 7; specific bonuses are not restated as percentages.
A new Soul Core socketable type added in 0.2.1. The confirmed count is 15; exact modifiers are unverified and described by category only.
Because these are brand-new item types, any filter written before 0.2.1 will hide or mis-handle them until you add entries, especially on console where filters are now supported.

sections.title: Why Item Filter needs new entries

items.title: New socketable types are invisible to old filters
items.detail: Runes, Talismans and Soul Cores did not exist before 0.2.1, so any filter authored earlier will not recognise them. Until you add explicit entries, these items can be hidden, shown as junk, or flagged incorrectly.

items.title: Console Item Filter support arrived in 0.2.1
items.detail: Console players gained Item Filter support in this patch. That makes the filter-entry gap a real problem on Xbox and PlayStation too: console players must add the new socketable rules or they will miss drops in their loot filter.

items.title: Socketables tie into existing currencies
items.detail: Because socketables interact with crafting and currency systems (for example Artificer-style sockets and related reagents), filter entries should cover both the socketables and the currencies used to manage them.

sections.title: Loot generation change: Item Class no longer weighed

changes.title: Unique drop no longer considers Item Class
changes.detail: Before 0.2.1 the Unique drop generation took Item Class into account when deciding what to drop. The patch removed that consideration, which rebalanced the spread of dropped Uniques across the item pool.

changes.title: Rings and Amulets more common
changes.detail: With Item Class no longer weighed, Rings and Amulets began dropping more often than they did under the old generation rules. This is a directional change, not a published percentage.

sections.title: Unique rarity pipeline: Mythic and Common shifts

changes.title: Mythic Unique drop increase
changes.detail: 0.2.1 increased the drop rate of Mythic Uniques, the top rarity tier. More of the most sought-after Uniques entered circulation, though the exact multiplier is not published in the notes.

changes.title: High-tier areas reduce Common Unique share
changes.detail: In higher-tier areas the share of Common Uniques was reduced, meaning top-end farming yields fewer low-value Uniques and relatively more interesting ones. This is described as a rule, not a printed number.

changes.title: Party Unique bonus reduced
changes.detail: The bonus that party play granted to Unique drops was reduced in 0.2.1. This narrows the gap between organized party farming and solo or small-group play, though the precise remaining bonus is not published.

changes.title: Solo play relatively stronger for Uniques
changes.detail: Because the party bonus shrank, solo and small-group players gained relative ground on Unique acquisition. Party play may still help for clear speed and survivability, but its Unique-drop edge is smaller than before 0.2.1.

changes.title: More Rings and Amulets reshape gear choices
changes.detail: With Rings and Amulets dropping more often, build guides that assumed a rare Unique ring or amulet should revisit how frequently those slots upgrade. The change is about availability, not stated numbers.

changes.title: Socketables open new crafting and scaling paths
changes.detail: The 22 Runes, 7 Talismans and 15 Soul Cores give crafters new slotted modifiers to chase, which can change how skill-granting and scaling Uniques, charms, and catalysts are valued in a build.

items.question: Why don't the new Runes and Soul Cores show in my Item Filter?
answer: They are new socketable types that did not exist before 0.2.1, so an older filter has no entries for them.
Add explicit Runes, Talismans and Soul Cores rules; on console, also turn on Item Filter support, which 0.2.1 introduced.

items.question: Is party play still better for Uniques after 0.2.1?
answer: The party Unique bonus was reduced, so the gap between party and solo play is smaller than before.
Party play may still help with clear speed and survival, but its Unique-drop edge is reduced; the exact remaining bonus is unverified.

items.question: What is a Mythic Unique?
answer: A Mythic Unique is the top rarity tier of Unique items.
0.2.1 increased the Mythic Unique drop rate, so more of these sought-after items enter circulation; the exact current rate is unverified.

items.question: Did Rings and Amulets drop more after 0.2.1?
answer: Yes. Because Unique drops no longer consider Item Class, Rings and Amulets became more common in the drop pool.
This is a directional rule change rather than a published percentage.

items.question: How many socketables did 0.2.1 actually add?
answer: 0.2.1 added 22 Endgame Runes, 7 Talismans, and 15 Soul Cores.
Those counts are the confirmed facts; individual socketable effects are described by category, not by published numbers.

items.question: Were the 0.2.1 loot changes a global rework?
answer: They changed the Unique drop pipeline rules: no Item Class weighting, a Mythic increase, reduced Common Unique share in high tiers, and a smaller party bonus.
Later patches may have retuned these; the current state in 0.5.4e is unverified, so treat the exact numbers as open.
